purpose: This medication is used to treat and prevent certain bacterial infections, including strep throat, syphilis, and rheumatic fever. It can also be used to prevent the return of rheumatic fever in people who have had it before. Your doctor may prescribe it for other types of bacterial infections as well.
how_it_works: Penicillin G Benzathine works by attacking the walls of bacteria, which causes them to break apart and die. It is given as a shot because it is slowly released into your body over days or weeks, giving you long-lasting protection. This slow release means you only need one shot instead of taking pills every day.
common_side_effects: Pain, swelling, or soreness at the injection site is the most common side effect. You might also experience nausea, diarrhea, or an upset stomach. Some people feel dizzy or develop a mild skin rash.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you have any signs of an allergic reaction, such as hives, difficulty breathing, swelling of your face or throat, or a fast heartbeat — this can be life-threatening. Let your doctor know if you have ever had an allergic reaction to any penicillin or cephalosporin antibiotic before. This medicine is given ONLY as a shot into the muscle — it must never be injected into a vein, as this can cause serious injury or death.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as a single injection into the muscle by a healthcare provider, usually in the buttock area. The dose and how often you get it depends on what infection is being treated. For strep throat, one shot is usually all that is needed, while for preventing rheumatic fever, shots may be given every 3 to 4 weeks on an ongoing basis.
